newsitem.title: SPAIN: Ecuador aims for 20 pct end-98 inflation-Davalos.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador aims for 20 pct end-98 inflation-Davalos.

text.p: Ecuador is aiming to bring inflation below 20 percent by the end of 1998, Finance Minister Carlos Davalos said on Tuesday.

"Among the main objectives we have set ourselves in managing our country's economy is implementing a fiscal policy in line with the goal of perservering in the fight against inflation, which we would like to bring down below 20 percent by the end of 1998," Davalos told the annual meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank.
Ecuadorian President Fabian Alarcon said in late February he saw 1998 inflation between 20 and 23 percent.
By the beginning of February 1997, inflation had risen to over 30 percent.

An interim government took power in February after President Abdala Bucaram was removed from the presidency just six months after he took office as corruption and drastic price increases sparked mass protests.
Congress appointed Alarcon as the interim president until elections in August 1998.

The interim government also plans to reduce the fiscal deficit to 2.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997. To do so, it has implemented fiscal austerity measures as well as making tax collection more effective.
"This should narrow the deficit to about 2.5 percent of GDP in 1997," Davalos said.
At the end of Bucaram's presidency, indicators had projected a 1997 fiscal deficit of about 6.5 percent of gross domestic product, he said.

"Though fully aware of the difficult situation facing the country, especially in the fiscal sphere, we were determined to overcome the crisis and restore confidence and credibility among domestic and foreign economic agents," Davalos said.
Davalos said the interim government was also aiming for GDP growth of 3.5 percent in 1997 and about four percent in 1998.
"These goals are consistent with the serious and transparent privatisation, capitalisation and concessions program being revived in our country," Davalos said.

"The programme is being carried out in telecommunications, with the sale of 35 percent of the shares of our national telecommunications company (EMETEL), and also involves highways concessions and the capitalisation of electric utilities," he said.
Davalos added that Alarcon's interim government remained committed to structural reform, to ensure confidence is restored among the international financial community.

"The government headed by President Fabian Alarcon is firmly resolved to go ahead with structural reforms, hand in hand with a modernisation of the state, economic globalisation and an awareness of the need to provide legal assurances to national and foreign investors, stimulate domestic savings and create jobs," Davalos said.
